terms.comment: Also any word (see word): Quintilian notes the two senses, every word of which speech is made, and the one part of speech, like legō, scrībō (1.5.2). Traupman’s definition, after the grammarians: pars ōrātiōnis cum tempore et persōnā sine cāsū (p. 225).

phrases.latin: verba nunc generāliter accipī volō, nam duplex eōrum intellēctus est; alter, quī omnia per quae sermō nectitur significat …; alter, in quō est ūna pars ōrātiōnis, legō, scrībō
phrases.english: I take ‘words’ here in the general sense, for the word has two meanings: one covers everything of which speech is woven, the other one part of speech, like legō, scrībō (I read, I write)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 220, 225, 249, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
